This PR implements the new recommended approach (https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/33302) on how to handle `ECONNRESET` during `clientError` events.

Fixes #2036.

issue_context.title: fastify behind haproxy results into "read ECONNRESET" errors
issue_context.body:
## 🐛 Bug Report

As mentioned in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/docs/Recommendations.md we would like to run fastify behind haproxy (for TLS termination and load balancing)

After processing an request proxied over haproxy it throws an ECONNRESET error:

```
{"level":30,"time":1578524093038,"pid":16376,"hostname":"ip-10-64-1-175","reqId":1,"req":{"method":"GET","url":"/check","hostname":"localhost","remoteAddress":"127.0.0.1","remotePort":42838},"msg":"incoming request","v":1}
{"level":30,"time":1578524093045,"pid":16376,"hostname":"ip-10-64-1-175","reqId":1,"res":{"statusCode":200},"responseTime":5.577713999897242,"msg":"request completed","v":1}
{"level":20,"time":1578524093046,"pid":16376,"hostname":"ip-10-64-1-175","err":{"type":"Error","message":"read ECONNRESET","stack":"Error: read ECONNRESET\n    at TCP.onStreamRead (internal/stream_base_commons.js:200:27)","errno":"ECONNRESET","code":"ECONNRESET","syscall":"read"},"msg":"client error","v":1}
{"level":30,"time":1578524101311,"pid":16376,"hostname":"ip-10-64-1-175","reqId":2,"req":{"method":"GET","url":"/check","hostname":"localhost","remoteAddress":"127.0.0.1","remotePort":42842},"msg":"incoming request","v":1}
{"level":30,"time":1578524101311,"pid":16376,"hostname":"ip-10-64-1-175","reqId":2,"res":{"statusCode":200},"responseTime":0.34771000035107136,"msg":"request completed","v":1}
{"level":20,"time":1578524101311,"pid":16376,"hostname":"ip-10-64-1-175","err":{"type":"Error","message":"read ECONNRESET","stack":"Error: read ECONNRESET\n    at TCP.onStreamRead (internal/stream_base_commons.js:200:27)","errno":"ECONNRESET","code":"ECONNRESET","syscall":"read"},"msg":"client error","v":1}
``` 

If I bypass haproxy and call directly the NodeJS process this is not happening:

```
{"level":30,"time":1578524117357,"pid":16376,"hostname":"ip-10-64-1-175","reqId":3,"req":{"method":"GET","url":"/check","hostname":"localhost:8337","remoteAddress":"127.0.0.1","remotePort":42850},"msg":"incoming request","v":1}
{"level":30,"time":1578524117357,"pid":16376,"hostname":"ip-10-64-1-175","reqId":3,"res":{"statusCode":200},"responseTime":0.4655680004507303,"msg":"request completed","v":1}
{"level":30,"time":1578524120839,"pid":16376,"hostname":"ip-10-64-1-175","reqId":4,"req":{"method":"GET","url":"/check","hostname":"localhost:8337","remoteAddress":"127.0.0.1","remotePort":42852},"msg":"incoming request","v":1}
{"level":30,"time":1578524120840,"pid":16376,"hostname":"ip-10-64-1-175","reqId":4,"res":{"statusCode":200},"responseTime":0.3121840003877878,"msg":"request completed","v":1}
```

Error is triggered via HTTP.Server 'clientError' - logged at https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/fastify.js#L417 - also I would ask why errors are just logged as "debug" severity?

## To Reproduce

To exclude other possible errors like network issues node and haproxy are running on the same machine.

As HTTP client for testing I used cmd line CURL on same machine. I could reproduce the same also with links & lynx browser on CMD line. Also it was reproducible from remote.

1. Node with fastify on Port 8337 (simple.ts)
2. Haproxy with haproxy.cfg on Port 80
3. "curl http://localhost/check" (over haproxy, causes that issue)
4. "curl http://localhost:8337/check" (directly NodeJS, no issue)

(Error is only logged on logger level >= debug)

*simple.ts*
```js
import * as fastify from 'fastify';

const app = fastify({
    logger: {
        level: 'trace',
    },
    trustProxy: true,
});

app.get('*', (_req, reply) => {
    reply.send('foo');
});

app.listen(8337, '0.0.0.0');
```

*haproxy.cfg* (reduced version out of Recommendations.md)
```haproxy
global
  log /dev/log syslog
  maxconn 4096
  chroot /var/lib/haproxy
  user haproxy
  group haproxy

defaults
  log   global
  mode  http
  option        httplog
  option        dontlognull
  option forwardfor
  retries       3
  option redispatch
  maxconn       2000
  timeout connect 5000
  timeout client 50000
  timeout server 50000

frontend proxy
  bind 0.0.0.0:80
  default_backend fastify

backend fastify
  server local 127.0.0.1:8337
```

## Expected behavior

I also tested if this also occurs with just node HTTP.server implementation, I couldn't reprodue it. Also I couldn't see this behavior with express.js.

There should be no "Error: read ECONNRESET\n    at TCP.onStreamRead"

Looks for me if something is trying to read on a already ended connection?

## Your Environment

- *node version*: 12.14.1
- *fastify version*: 2.11.0
- *os*: Linux, debian buster - also reproduced on Mac
- *haproxy version*: 1.8.19-1+deb10u1
- *curl version*: 7.64.0
- *any other relevant information*
comments:
That is a debug error because it happens on a truncated socket. Your HAPRoxy is maintaining a live connection to the server which times out at 50s (from your config), which results in `clientError` to be emitted and that error logged at debug level - it's not a real error, but something that you might want to triage/diagnose.

You can get the same value from express or node core by listening to the `'clientError'` event.
You probably want to add `option http-server-close` to the `defaults` section. This should also be added to the example config in the recommendations doc. Would you care to send a PR @xpender?

I am having the same issue. However, in my case, this problem occurs when a fastify server is uploaded to kubernetes on the cloud as pod, not on the local haproxy.

The following article may be little related, and the problem is that this happens when the fastify server runs behind proxy. (Of course, I'm using a version of kubernetes where the following issue is resolved.)
https://kubernetes.io/blog/2019/03/29/kube-proxy-subtleties-debugging-an-intermittent-connection-reset/

And if I change the coding to the express server in the same environment, I don't get an error. I want to know what the exact reason is. @mcollina

@gtolarc Are you trying to capture the `'clientError'` in express? Can you confirm that is not emitted? Uploading the express vs fastify code would be interesting.

---

To provide a bit more context

>  also I would ask why errors are just logged as "debug" severity?

Because this is not an error. Essentially there is nothing a developer can do as the socket get truncated for whatever reason. Increasing the level will be confusing for most people.

In fact, there are a lot of places that use Kubernetes these days, and even during development, debug logs are turned on and put on the cloud for testing. People like me who are trying to fastify for the first time will be confused from the beginning..

The problem is that it’s impossible to know if those are legit problems or not without looking at them. If there are a lot, they imply that there is something to be fixed in the proxy. Even if they happen, they are not really causing production issues.

Fastify is doing the correct thing in logging these out.

I am using ali cloud's managed kubernates service, and even if I create a new kubernates cluster and upload the basic example of the fastify server as pod, the ECONNRESET error occurs immediately in large quantities.

There may be problems with the proxy, so detecting clientError events by default seems to confuse users like me.
I think we should move that log messages to the `.trace` level, and then investigate what config needs to be placed in Kubernetes to avoid this.
Thanks @wopol! I think it makes things pretty clear if increasing the headers make it reliable. We should just document why this is happening and how to fix (increase the headers limit).
I have this issue saved to my notifications to address with a PR to the recommendation doc. I _might_ get to it this weekend.

While debugging this issue, I think the problem is actually in Node.js itself.

I've tried executing this sample server:

```javascript
const { createServer } = require('http');

const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    res.writeHead(200, {'Content-Length': 2}).end('OK');
})

server.on('clientError', (err, socket) => {
    console.log('CLIENT ERROR');
    socket.end('HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request\r\n\r\n');
});

server.listen(8331);
```

With the following haproxy configuration:

```
global
  log stdout format raw local1
  maxconn 4096

defaults
  log   global
  mode  http
  option        httplog
  option        dontlognull
  option forwardfor
  retries       3
  option redispatch
  maxconn       2000
  timeout connect 5000
  timeout client 50000
  timeout server 50000

frontend proxy
  bind 0.0.0.0:8330
  default_backend fastify

backend fastify
  server local 127.0.0.1:8331
````

As you can see, neither haproxy neither node are sending a FIN packet. Haproxy instead sends a RST which results in the client error on the node side.

I've filed the following issue in Node to address the problem: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/33302

Hope this helps!
